Messages.Author: Izaak
Messages.Body:
This came up in a for-fun game after the third round of a tournament:
 
Does Burst of Sunlight affect retainers? The new card text is pretty clear in saying "1R Aggravated", but also suggests that you have to target it, meaning you can kill a Raven Spy at inferior with it, OR target the opposing vampire.
 
The OLD card text, kinda suggests it's an overall effect that just "everything" in combat gets the damage, much like weather control.
 
I admit, we didn't have a new card handy so that's probably why it came up in the first place. Am I correct in assuming that it's a single-target strike that just happens to be aggravated and hurt yourself as well, like the card-text suggests?

rfg...@eos.ncsu.edu:

> > IMO non-vampires should be immune to any damage from this card.

> If you applied the rules of the game based on card title, you would

ok, some points to support my argument:
- this game is about vampires, vampires don't, in general, like to
sunbathe.
- other creatures than vampires appear in the game, most of them don't
mind a bit of sun, many even like it.
- the 'theme' of the card (based on the power from the rpg), as I
understand it, is that the vampires in the combat are exposed to
artificial (iirc) sunlight. that is the effect the original cardtext
had (only on vampires).
- the card was reworded, IMO this could have been done better.

I am aware that this is a card game and is not the same as the rpg and
balance should have higher priority than mood. but as I have said in
other threads, it is still based on the rpg and where viable should
try to maintain the mood of the rpg. killing ravens with a ray of
sunshine does not maintain the mood and I can't see any reason how not
being able to kill retainers with sunlight is a threat to game
balance.

> That's why they invented card text.

[sarcasm]well that was a mistake, we should only use the titles of the
cards.[/sarcasm]

> However, to induldge your argument-- I get sunburned, don't you?

I do actually, not as badly as a vampire would though :-)

bad sunburn (where skin peels of) actually helps you survive heavy
sunshine, as what is happening is that cells that are badly mutated
because of UV rays commit suicide (apoptosis). if they don't do that
(and are still damaged) they can potentially transform into cancer
cells, which are not good for you (as most people know), but that
death/damage takes a while to bring somone down.

vampire 'sunburn' is not a protective mechanism... erm... for vampires
anyway.

You get it, but you don't. You act sarcastic in the above quote, but
in the previous two paragraphs you take on the topic of vampires and
sunlight in a very non sarcastic way. The only place that mentions
sunlight is the card title. Try calling the card "That Not So Fresh
Feeling" and look at it again.

There's nothing else to suggest that allies/retainers should be immune
to damage from this card, but not immune to a card like Thrown Sewer
Lid.

Switching to the non card game world:

> > However, to induldge your argument-- I get sunburned, don't you?
>
> I do actually, not as badly as a vampire would though :-)
>
> bad sunburn (where skin peels of) actually helps you survive heavy
> sunshine, as what is happening is that cells that are badly mutated
> because of UV rays commit suicide (apoptosis). if they don't do that
> (and are still damaged) they can potentially transform into cancer
> cells, which are not good for you (as most people know), but that
> death/damage takes a while to bring somone down.
>
> vampire 'sunburn' is not a protective mechanism... erm... for vampires
> anyway.

The cancer thing is a straw man. Sunburn is still painful. Serious
sunburn can require hospitalization. That's real damage.

You argue that allies should be immune from the card effects because
sunlight isn't harmful to them, but you admit that it is harmful to
human beings. The real world logic doesn't hold up here.

--Rob Grau

--------------------------
summary:

mood is important.
balance is more important.
optimal solution is when both are maintained.

if a part of cards effect is threat to balance, that part should be
changed while trying to maintain the mood. other parts of the cards
effect than the one that is a threat to bame balance should remain
unchanged.

if you disagree... well then we disagree. to bad (or is it?)

When I look at the newsgroup archives, it looks like the rules team
decided to change the way damage that allies received when playing
cards "as a vampire" in May 2002. My guess is those rulings were
related to the rewording of Burst of Sunlight when the Camarilla
Edition was released in August 2002. You really need to ask LSJ or a
rules team member what their rational was before you build an argument
that it was all done because of game balance. I don't know.

> from having this card not being able to hurt allies. there may have
> been other complications with the original text, but this solution was
> IMO not the best one. (now... try to understand that this is the main
> point of what I am trying to explain here).

Well, I'm not going to change your opinion. However, If your opinion
was based on rules or a game mechanic, then I'd probably care a lot
more about it.

> > Switching to the non card game world:
> <snip bunch of irrelevant stuff>
> > The cancer thing is a straw man. Sunburn is still painful. Serious
> > sunburn can require hospitalization. That's real damage.
>

> exposure does it take for you to be aware of the damage?

I'd say that by the end of strike resolution, you'd know. :)

> > You argue that allies should be immune from the card effects because
> > sunlight isn't harmful to them, but you admit that it is harmful to
> > human beings. The real world logic doesn't hold up here.
>
> it is damaging yes, but not in such a way that it would cause anyone
> to die/be severly injured for the duration of the fight he was
> involved in at the moment when he was exposed to the sunlight. so that
> logic does hold.

If that's the way you want it to be, then sure. I only wanted to get
across the point that sunlight wasn't completely harmless, since
that's what the original statement was.

I don't see why any decent storyteller couldn't work through this
issue. Who says it has to be regular sunlight? The "Burst" is
really created through Thamaturgy, so I don't see why it couldn't be
more concentrated or more potent sunlight. I mean it's not like
anyone has actually shown up with a light meter and asked a Tremere to
cast the Burst of Sunlight spell.

> if you disagree... well then we disagree. to bad (or is it?)

Indeed.

--Rob Grau
